content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], Where can I find details about these limitations? After two days of researching technical documents, I haven't found a clear explanation. Is the restriction due to Modbus, Profinet, or another communication protocol? What would you suggest as a solution? There hasn't been any alternative provided yet. 1) Upgrade to a higher-level HMI? 2) Use a full-featured PLC to aggregate data from [product_name]? 3) Avoid using [product_name] altogether? 4) Consider an open architecture alternative? Thank you.
This is a limitation of the Basic Panel version. A higher-level HMI can support up to 8 simultaneous connections. I only have information available in German.

If you want to connect more than four [product_name] modules to a Basic Panel, you must designate four of them as data collectors. For higher-level HMIs, up to eight modules can act as data collectors.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are evaluating the connection restrictions of a Basic Panel when connecting multiple automation modules. They are unclear whether the limitation of four simultaneous connections arises from hardware, firmware, or the communication protocol. The discussion highlights frustration about the lack of transparent documentation and calls for alternatives such as hardware upgrades, architectural changes, or switching the control platform.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to connect more than four automation modules to a Basic Panel and to access clear documentation about the source of these restrictions. They also seek well-explained alternative solutions for bypassing these limits.
